examples.en: I take care of my father at the hospital every day.
I took leave from work to look after my mother.
It isn't easy for family to nurse a patient directly.
We are looking for someone to care for the patient.
My older brother nursed Grandma all night.
I'm truly grateful to the person who cares for the patient.

explain: 아픈 사람 곁에서 먹이고 씻기고 돌보는 일을 말해요. 의사나 간호사의 치료인 '치료하다'와 달리 생활을 도와주는 돌봄이에요. '간병인', '간병비'처럼 사람이나 돈 이야기에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means staying beside a sick person to feed, wash and look after them. Unlike '치료하다', the treatment by doctors and nurses, it is daily-life caregiving. It also appears in related words like '간병인' (caregiver) and '간병비' (care costs).

examples.ko: 할머니가 다리를 다치셔서 혼자 거동하기 힘드세요.
examples.en: My grandmother hurt her leg, so it is hard for her to move around alone.

examples.ko: 거동이 불편하신 할머니를 병원까지 모셔다 드렸어요.
examples.en: I took my grandmother, who has difficulty moving around, to the hospital.

examples.ko: 수술 후에는 일주일 동안 거동하지 마세요.
examples.en: Please do not move around for a week after the surgery.

examples.ko: 아버지는 이제 지팡이 없이도 거동하실 수 있어요.
examples.en: My father can now get around even without a cane.

examples.ko: 환자가 거동할 수 있을 때까지 옆에서 도와줘야 해요.
examples.en: We have to help the patient until he can move around.
Seeing the way you move around, you have gotten a lot better.

explain: 주로 '거동이 불편하다'처럼 노인이나 환자의 몸 움직임에 써요. 높일 때는 '거동하시다'라고 해요. 일상 대화에서는 '움직이다'나 '돌아다니다'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in '거동이 불편하다' for the body movement of elderly or sick people. To be respectful, say '거동하시다'. In daily talk people more often say '움직이다' or '돌아다니다'.

examples.ko: 그는 결벽증이 있어서 손을 하루에 수십 번 씻어요.
examples.en: He has a cleanliness obsession, so he washes his hands dozens of times a day.

examples.ko: 결벽증 때문에 남이 쓴 컵은 못 써요.
examples.en: Because of my cleanliness obsession, I cannot use a cup someone else used.
My roommate cleans at an obsessive level.

examples.ko: 저는 결벽증은 아니지만 정리는 꼭 해야 해요.
examples.en: I am not obsessive about cleanliness, but I must tidy up.

examples.ko: 결벽증으로 보일 만큼 깨끗하게 사는 친구예요.
examples.en: My friend lives so cleanly that it looks like an obsession.
My friend says I am a clean freak.

explain: 깔끔한 정도를 넘어서 더러운 것을 지나치게 싫어하는 사람에게 쓰는 말이에요. 가볍게 '나 결벽증인가 봐'라고 농담으로도 하지만, 다른 사람에게 직접 말하면 기분이 상할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes someone who goes beyond tidy and is excessively bothered by dirt. People joke '나 결벽증인가 봐' about themselves, but saying it directly to another person can offend them.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마 손을 꼭 그러쥐고 놓지 않아요.
examples.en: The child grips her mom's hand tightly and won't let go.
It was cold, so I walked with both fists clenched.

examples.ko: 그는 화가 나서 주먹을 불끈 그러쥐었어요.
examples.en: He was angry and clenched his fist hard.

examples.ko: 동전을 손에 그러쥔 채 가게로 뛰어갔어요.
examples.en: I ran to the store with the coins clutched in my hand.
I was nervous and was gripping the hem of my clothes.

examples.ko: 아기가 제 손가락을 그러쥐니까 너무 귀여워요.
examples.en: It's so cute when the baby grips my finger.

explain: '잡다', '쥐다'보다 손에 힘을 주어 꽉 움켜잡는 느낌이 강해요. 주먹을 쥐거나 손에 든 것을 꼭 잡을 때 쓰고, 말보다는 글에서 더 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than '잡다' or '쥐다', as if you squeeze hard with your hand. It is used for clenching a fist or holding something tightly, and you will see it more in writing than in speech.

examples.en: I starched the shirt and ironed it stiff.
I was so startled that my body went stiff.

examples.ko: 새 와이셔츠 깃이 빳빳이 서 있어요.
examples.en: The collar of the new dress shirt stands stiff.
He walked off with his head held stiffly high.

examples.ko: 햇볕에 널어 둔 수건이 빳빳이 말랐어요.
examples.en: The towel I hung in the sun dried stiff.
Please sit on the chair with your back held straight.

explain: '빳빳하다'에서 온 부사로, 구부러지지 않고 곧고 뻣뻣한 모습을 말해요. '빳빳하게'라고도 많이 말해요. '고개를 빳빳이 들다'는 겸손하지 않고 당당하거나 거만한 태도를 나타낼 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It is the adverb form of '빳빳하다' and describes something staying straight and stiff without bending. People also often say '빳빳하게'. '고개를 빳빳이 들다' can also show a proud or arrogant attitude.

examples.en: I sterilize baby bottles in boiling water.

examples.ko: 우유는 높은 온도에서 살균한 뒤 팔아요.
examples.en: Milk is sterilized at a high temperature before it is sold.
Please sterilize the knife and cutting board with hot water.
Don't drink water that hasn't been sterilized.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 자외선으로 공기를 살균해 줘요.
examples.en: This machine sterilizes the air with ultraviolet light.
Hospitals always sterilize their instruments before use.

explain: 세균을 죽인다는 점에서 '소독하다'와 가깝지만, '살균하다'는 우유·물·기구처럼 세균을 없애는 과정을 말할 때 자주 써요. '소독하다'는 상처, 손, 방처럼 더 넓은 대상에 써요. 명사 '살균'은 '살균 우유'처럼 붙여 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '소독하다' in that both involve killing germs, but '살균하다' is often used for the process of removing germs from things like milk, water and instruments. '소독하다' covers a wider range, such as wounds, hands and rooms. The noun '살균' is used in terms like '살균 우유'.

examples.en: After going up and down the stairs, my knees ache.
My elbow joint was sore, so I went to the hospital.
My wrist aches, but it's bearable.
I put a pain patch on my aching shoulder.

examples.ko: 찬 바람을 맞으면 이가 시큰거리기 시작해요.
examples.en: When I'm hit by cold wind, my teeth start to feel sensitive.
Watching the sad movie, my nose stung with emotion.

explain: 관절이나 이가 시리고 저린 듯한 약한 통증이 계속될 때 써요. 슬프거나 감동받았을 때 코끝이 찡한 느낌에도 비유해서 써요. 같은 느낌을 '시큰하다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: It describes a mild, lingering sore or stinging feeling in joints or teeth. It is also used figuratively for the stinging feeling in your nose when you are sad or moved. The same feeling can be expressed with '시큰하다'.

examples.ko: 피부가 물질에 접촉하면 가려울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If skin touches the substance, it can get itchy.

examples.ko: 환자와 접촉한 사람은 검사를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: People who had contact with the patient must get tested.
I tried making contact with that company.
After touching animals, I wash my hands.

examples.ko: 외국인과 접촉하는 일이 많아서 영어가 필요해요.
examples.en: I meet foreigners a lot at work, so I need English.
Two wires touched and sparks flew.

explain: '접촉하다'는 몸이나 물건이 닿는 것뿐 아니라 사람이나 회사와 연락을 시작하는 것에도 써요. 가볍게 손을 대는 것은 '만지다'가 일상에서 더 자연스러워요. 뉴스에서는 '접촉자', '접촉 사고'처럼 명사로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 접촉하다 covers physical contact and also starting contact with a person or company. For lightly touching with the hand, 만지다 is more natural in daily talk. In news it appears as nouns such as 접촉자 (a contact) and 접촉 사고 (minor collision).
